cands.bio: Democrat who has represented Alabama House District 83 (Opelika) since November 2018. Born in Opelika, graduated from N.C. State in sports management, and founded the small business Elevate Your Grind Inc. Ran unsuccessfully for Congress (AL-2) in the 2024 Democratic primary.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving a 2026 voter-guide recommendation from the 92% Club (Sway voting group by Kenya Anissa).

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions from Gray on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, policing and public-order penalties, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site says he passed bills on lifting the K-12 yoga ban, a 180-day grace period for paying fines and fees, and a small-business innovation matching fund, but we found no legislative record confirming them. We also found no source for his birth date, when he left Alabama for college and football, or the full list of bills he has sponsored. His campaign site says he is Minority Whip of the House Democratic Caucus, but we found no independent confirmation. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys.

qual.background: Has served in the Alabama House since November 2018, winning re-election in 2022 and 2026. Also a small business owner (founder of Elevate Your Grind Inc.) with a bachelor's degree in sports management.
qual.why: More than seven years of legislative service is the main factor, together with business ownership. Ballotpedia does not list any law, policy or budget career, and the leadership post he claims on his campaign site is not confirmed there.

pro-life.evidence: His 2024 congressional campaign site says he supports abortion access and would oppose mandatory waiting periods, TRAP laws and gestational bans. It also says he would support funding for Planned Parenthood.

second-amendment.evidence: His 2024 congressional campaign site says he would champion universal background checks and a ban on assault weapons with high-capacity magazines. It also says he has opposed what it calls extreme Republican gun laws in the state House.
